letters.title: On the Nature of Time
letters.opening: A thought on the passing of time.
body: There is something peculiar about time. We spend so much of it waiting for what comes next, only to find ourselves looking back at what has already passed.
Perhaps the greatest tragedy is not that time moves so quickly, but that we so often forget to be present while it does.
letters.author: M.

letters.title: The Art of Being Alone
body: There is a difference between being alone and feeling lonely. One is a circumstance, the other a state of mind.
Perhaps we ought to learn to enjoy our own company before asking the world to keep us company.
letters.author: M.

letters.title: On the Things Left Unsaid
letters.opening: A letter about words we never speak.
body: Some words remain with us long after the moment in which they should have been spoken has passed.
I wonder how many conversations have existed only in the minds of those who were too afraid to begin them.
letters.author: M.
